function: MARL jointly selects each UAV's communication transmit power and 2D motion to trade off sensing mutual information, UAV-to-BS data rate, energy and flight safety. p. 3-5.
system: Two BSs, one UAV each at 20 m sensing 16 vehicles; mmWave links (1 cm wavelength) modeled by antenna gains only; no RIS. p. 2, 5.
method: Distributed multi-agent double DQN (DMADDQN): centralized training, distributed execution, shared experience memory, MSE loss, Adam, epsilon-greedy; reinforcement learning. p. 4-5.
data_channel: Own simulator: free-space communication SNR, radar-equation sensing SNR; 16 vehicles on a 400 m intersection; no 3GPP or measured channel. p. 2-3, 5.
test_conditions: Same simulated scenario; tests sweep vehicle speed (2 to 10 m/s) and reward weights w1, w3; whether retrained per value is not stated. p. 5.
baselines: Learned only: centralized multi-agent DQN (CMADQN) and DDQN (CMADDQN); no non-learned baseline. p. 5.
metrics: Average total reward, average number of sensing users, communication data rate, sensing mutual information, energy-saving factor, minimum inter-UAV distance. p. 5-6.
complexity: none; only a qualitative remark that distributed execution lowers the learning difficulty. p. 5.
openness: none; no code or data link, simulation only. p. 5.
q1_support: p. 3: "the communication SNR between UAV i and BS m is" - free-space formula (6) with antenna gains, sensing by radar equation (3, p. 2); no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 5: "schemes perform better than other schemes under different conditions" - speed sweep in Fig. 4 and weight sweeps in Figs. 5-6; the paper never says a policy trained at one setting is tested at another.
q3_support: p. 5: "We consider using centralized multi-agent DQN (CMADQN) and DDQN (CMADDQN)" - only learned benchmarks, which are centralized versions of the proposed agent; no non-learned baseline such as random, fixed or optimization-based control.
q4_support: p. 5: "so the learning difficulty is lower than the centralized strategies" - qualitative statement only; no complexity order, FLOPs, parameters or runtime anywhere.
q5_support: p. 5: "We consider that the study area of the simulation is" - own simulated scenario; no code or data link and no public dataset.
notes: Research letter. Included under the aerial-link rule: the policy learns UAV transmit power (physical layer) jointly with UAV motion (above physical layer), p. 3-4. Areas 5 and 6 both fit (a UAV link that also senses); area 6 wins by the order of the instructions, and the link is modeled only by antenna gains, so it is a single-antenna-type link, admitted for area 6. If the reviewer prefers area 5, the system rule would exclude the work. q2 is 0 because the speed sweep (Fig. 4) is not stated to test a policy trained elsewhere. Figures and algorithm read from page images of pages 2, 4, 5 and 6.
